Let  
\[
a_n=\psi(3^n).
\]
Using \(x=3^n\) in the functional equation,
\[
a_{n+1}+3a_n=a_n^3,
\]
so
\[
a_{n+1}=a_n^3-3a_n.
\]
Also,
\[
a_0=\psi(1)=\sqrt{2+\sqrt{2+\sqrt2}}=2\cos\frac{\pi}{16}.
\]
Using
\[
(2\cos\theta)^3-3(2\cos\theta)=2\cos(3\theta),
\]
we get by induction
\[
a_n=2\cos\left(\frac{3^n\pi}{16}\right).
\]

The sequence has period \(8\) because \(3^8\equiv 1\pmod{32}\). Let \(c_k=\cos\frac{k\pi}{16}\). The first 8 terms for \(n=1,\dots,8\) are
\[
2c_3,\ 2c_9,\ 2c_5,\ -2c_1,\ -2c_3,\ -2c_9,\ -2c_5,\ 2c_1.
\]
Thus
\[
P_8=\prod_{n=1}^8 a_n=2^8(c_1c_3c_5c_9)^2
=2^8(c_1c_3c_5c_7)^2.
\]
Using
\[
c_1c_3c_5c_7=\frac{1}{8\sqrt2},
\]
we get
\[
P_8=2^8\cdot \frac1{128}=2.
\]
Also,
\[
P_4=\prod_{n=1}^4 a_n
=(2c_3)(2c_9)(2c_5)(-2c_1)
=16(c_1c_3c_5c_7)=\sqrt2.
\]
Since \(100=12\cdot 8+4\),
\[
\prod_{n=1}^{100}\psi(3^n)=P_8^{12}P_4=2^{12}\sqrt2=4096\sqrt2.
\]

The answer is \(4096\sqrt{2}\).
